$comment: Every desktop and window manager the configurator offers. The generator writes `module.config` into the host's configuration.nix, so adding one is a data change. Special values: {"$path": "./x"} is a path in the host flake, {"$context": "users"} the users' names, {"$context": "configDir"} where the host flake lives. `checks.desktops` verifies every nixpkgs option path here exists. `unavailable` marks one that can't be installed with this nixpkgs (it doesn't evaluate or build; nix/screenshots finds out) and says why: it's shown but can't be picked. `graphics` is what its whole session (compositor, shell, its own apps) needs: to start, or for its core UI to draw, `gl` and/or `gles` (minimum OpenGL / OpenGL ES versions, either will do) and `vulkan` (true: needed too), with `why` when that isn't plain; to draw everything on the GPU, `full` (any of `gl`, `gles`, `vulkan`: a Vulkan GPU, not lavapipe), below which the part `onCpu` names draws on the CPU; `source` says where it comes from; `{}` needs no GPU. The installer detects the machine's (engine status::graphics), greys out what can't start there and warns where part of it would draw on the CPU (docs/graphics.md).

desktops.name: COSMIC

graphics.source: cosmic-comp 1.2.0 needs only OpenGL ES 2.0 (smithay gles/mod.rs:612-623), but Settings, Files, Terminal, Editor and its portal draw with wgpu 28. Its OpenGL adapter needs OpenGL 3.3 (wgpu-hal gles/adapter.rs:257-277); without one it takes lavapipe (iced_wgpu window/compositor.rs:198-225, wgpu-core instance.rs:469-538), where iced's shaders need F16C, which Core 2-era CPUs lack (wgpu-hal vulkan/adapter.rs:1916-1922, Mesa gallivm/lp_bld_limits.h:81-84), and panic (VM-tested on a Core 2's instruction set; ICED_BACKEND=tiny-skia avoids it). With OpenGL 3.3 but no storage buffers (crocus Gen6, R600, Tesla) and no Vulkan GPU the device request fails and they draw with tiny-skia on the CPU (iced_renderer fallback.rs:273-335). The panel, applets, launcher and lock screen always use tiny-skia
